title: Language Models Show a "Women-Are-Wonderful" Effect in Blame Attribution That is Not Just Leniency
abstract: arXiv:2610.41116v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper investigates the Women-Are-Wonderful (WaW) effect in language-model blame attribution: a favorable bias in which women receive more positive evaluations than men. Using 11,270 interpersonal conflicts from r/AmItheAsshole, we construct matched counterfactuals that vary the gender of the person being judged (the original poster) and the person affected (the counter-party). Across four language models, gender changes a minority of verdicts, but those changes consistently favor women. The effect is strongly role-dependent. Making the original poster a woman reduces the odds of blame by 9--52%, while making the counter-party a woman multiplies them by 2.7--9.2X. Counter-party WaW also varies across conflict types, strengthening in communication and relationship conflicts and weakening in family conflicts. Exploratory probes suggest that counter-party gender can shift judgments of sympathy, reasonableness, harm and protection. WaW i

translated_title: 语言模型在归因责备中表现出“女性很美好”效应，且不仅仅是宽容
translated_abstract: 本文研究了语言模型在归因责备中的“女性很美好”效应：这是一种有利偏见，即女性比男性获得更多的积极评价。我们利用来自 r/AmItheAsshole 的 11,270 个人际冲突案例，构建了匹配的反事实样本，改变被评判者（发帖人）和受影响者（对方）的性别。在四个语言模型中，性别改变了一小部分判定结果，但这些变化一致地偏向女性。该效应强烈依赖于角色：将发帖人设为女性会使被责备的几率降低 9%-52%，而将对方设为女性会使该几率增加 2.7-9.2 倍。对方的 WaW 效应也因冲突类型而异，在沟通和关系冲突中增强，在家庭冲突中减弱。探索性探测表明，对方的性别可以改变模型对同情心、合理性、伤害和保护等方面的判断。
tldr: 该研究发现语言模型在人际冲突的责备归因中存在角色依赖的“女性很美好”效应：将受影响方设为女性会使被责备几率增加 2.7-9.2 倍，而将被评判方设为女性则使被责备几率降低 9%-52%。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a strongly role-dependent "Women-Are-Wonderful" effect in language model blame attribution: making the counter-party female multiplies blame odds by 2.7-9.2X, while making the original poster female reduces them by 9-52%.
